title: Functions Programming Models: In-Process vs Isolated
description: Understand the two programming models in Azure Functions and how to choose the right one for your project.

data.text: Azure Functions offers two programming models: the in-process model and the isolated worker model. The model you choose affects your project's dependencies, startup behavior, and flexibility.
The in-process model runs your function code inside the Azure Functions host process. It is the original model and provides the simplest experience.

items: Function code runs inside the Functions host
Tight integration with the host for better performance
Supported on all extensions and bindings

data.text: The isolated worker model runs your function code in a separate process from the Functions host. It gives you full control over the app's dependencies and startup.

items: Function code runs in its own process
Full control over dependencies and middleware

cards.title: In-Process
cards.description: Code runs inside the Functions host.

cards.title: Isolated Worker
cards.description: Code runs in a separate process.

data.title: Recommendation
data.text: For new .NET projects, use the isolated worker model. It provides the most flexibility and aligns with modern .NET patterns.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: In-process model runs inside the Functions host
Isolated worker model runs in a separate process
Isolated worker offers more control and flexibility
New projects should use the isolated worker model
data.takeaway: Choose isolated worker for new .NET Azure Functions projects.
